title: pkix-chain use-case wrappers hardwire DefaultVerifier, cannot use custom crypto
description:
All eight use-case wrappers in pkix-chain (verify_tls_server, verify_tls_client_dns, verify_tls_client_mailbox, verify_smime_signer, verify_smime_recipient, verify_code_signer, verify_time_stamper, verify_ocsp_responder) hardwire DefaultVerifier as the signature verifier. The doc comments on each function note this: 'The signature verifier is hardwired to DefaultVerifier. Callers that need a custom verifier should drop down to verify_chain.'

This means any caller needing FIPS-validated crypto, HSM-backed signatures, Ed25519, P-521, RSA-PSS, or any algorithm not in DefaultVerifier's dispatch table cannot use the use-case wrappers. They must replicate the identity-binding and profile-enforcement logic themselves when dropping to verify_chain.

What goes wrong if this stays as-is: The use-case wrappers are the ergonomic, documented API for common verification patterns. Callers with custom crypto are excluded from them and must write equivalent boilerplate. The identity binding (pkix_identity::verify_dns_name/verify_mailbox), the post-validation checks (timestamping EKU criticality, OCSP delegation), and the nocheck shim logic are all non-trivial and error-prone to replicate.

A generic V: SignatureVerifier parameter on the wrappers (alongside the existing P: Profile and R: RevocationChecker generics) would eliminate this forcing function without changing the zero-cost-for-default-crypto ergonomics (callers using DefaultVerifier would type-infer it).

Locations: All wrapper functions in /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-chain/src/lib.rs (lines 781-1324)
